comment: The 'From' email address for the Custom Email 1 store identity.
modal: The sender email address used when the **Custom Email 1** identity is selected as the sender of a transactional email. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' display name for the Custom Email 1 store identity.
modal: The sender name shown on emails sent from the **Custom Email 1** identity. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' email address for the Custom Email 2 store identity.
modal: The sender email address used when the **Custom Email 2** identity is selected as the sender of a transactional email. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' display name for the Custom Email 2 store identity.
modal: The sender name shown on emails sent from the **Custom Email 2** identity. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' email address for the General Contact store identity.
modal: The sender email address for the **General Contact** identity, the default sender for many store notifications. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' display name for the General Contact store identity.
modal: The sender name shown on emails sent from the **General Contact** identity. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' email address for the Sales Representative store identity.
modal: The sender email address for the **Sales Representative** identity, used as the sender of sales-related emails. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' display name for the Sales Representative store identity.
modal: The sender name shown on emails sent from the **Sales Representative** identity. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' email address for the Customer Support store identity.
modal: The sender email address for the **Customer Support** identity, used as the sender of support-related emails. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The 'From' display name for the Customer Support store identity.
modal: The sender name shown on emails sent from the **Customer Support** identity. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: Shows the template file path of each block on storefront pages for debugging.
modal: When **Yes**, storefront pages are overlaid with the path of the `.phtml` template rendering each block, to help locate markup. A development aid; keep **No** in production. Can differ per store view.

comment: Shows the template file path of each block on Admin pages for debugging.
modal: When **Yes**, Admin pages display the path of the `.phtml` template rendering each block. A development aid; keep **No** in production.

comment: Adds each block's PHP class name alongside the template path hints.
modal: When **Yes**, the template path hints also show the PHP block class that renders each template. Only meaningful while template path hints are enabled. Can differ per store view.

comment: Enables in-place editing of storefront translations directly on the page.
modal: When **Yes**, translatable strings on the storefront can be edited inline by an authorised user. A translation/development aid; keep **No** in production. Can differ per store view.

comment: Combines JavaScript files into fewer requests to speed up page loads.
modal: When **Yes**, the storefront's JavaScript files are merged into fewer files to reduce HTTP requests. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

comment: Bundles JavaScript modules together to reduce the number of requests.
modal: When **Yes**, JavaScript is bundled for the storefront to cut request count. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

comment: Combines CSS files into fewer requests to speed up page loads.
modal: When **Yes**, the storefront's CSS files are merged into fewer files to reduce HTTP requests. A production performance option. Can differ per store view.

comment: Appends a version to static asset URLs so browsers fetch fresh files after a deploy.
modal: When **Yes**, static files are served with a signature/version in their URL, forcing clients to reload updated assets after each deployment instead of serving stale cached copies.

comment: Which countries customers may select in address and checkout forms.
modal: The set of countries offered in country dropdowns across the store (registration, checkout, addresses). Can differ per website.

comment: The country selected by default in address and checkout forms.
modal: The pre-selected country in country dropdowns. Can differ per website or store view, so each store can default to its primary market.

comment: Which countries are treated as part of the European Union.
modal: The list of countries the store treats as EU members, used by EU-specific logic such as VAT handling.

comment: Countries listed at the top of country dropdowns as quick-pick destinations.
modal: Countries pinned to the top of country selectors as frequently used destinations, ahead of the full alphabetical list. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The time zone used for storing and displaying store dates and times.
modal: The time zone applied to the store's dates and times (orders, reports, schedules). Can differ per website.

comment: The language/locale used for the store's interface and formatting.
modal: The locale that sets the store's language and number/date formatting. Can differ per website or store view, so each store can run in its own language.

comment: Which weekday calendars treat as the first day of the week.
modal: The day shown first in calendar controls (e.g. Sunday or Monday). Can differ per website or store view to match local convention.

comment: Which days are treated as the weekend.
modal: The days marked as weekend, used by date-based logic. Can differ per website or store view to match local convention.

comment: The store name shown in transactional emails, invoices and similar documents.
modal: The store's name as it appears in customer-facing templates such as email headers and printed documents. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The store contact phone number shown in emails and documents.
modal: The store phone number displayed in customer-facing templates such as emails and invoices. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The store's hours of operation shown in emails and documents.
modal: Free-text hours of operation displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The store's country, used in emails, documents and address formatting.
modal: The country of the store's registered address, shown in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

comment: The store's region or state, shown in emails and documents.
modal: The region/state of the store's address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

comment: The store's ZIP/postal code, shown in emails and documents.
modal: The postal code of the store's address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

comment: The store's city, shown in emails and documents.
modal: The city of the store's address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

comment: The store's street address, shown in emails and documents.
modal: The first line of the store's street address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

comment: The second line of the store's street address, shown in emails and documents.
modal: An optional second line of the store's street address, displayed in customer-facing templates. Can differ per website.

comment: The store's VAT registration number, shown on applicable documents.
modal: The merchant's VAT registration number, displayed in customer-facing templates such as invoices where required. Can differ per website.

comment: Stops the store from sending any outbound email.
modal: When **Yes**, all outbound email from the store is suppressed. Useful on staging/testing environments to avoid emailing real customers. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: How outbound mail is sent — via Sendmail or an SMTP server.
modal: Selects the mail transport: **Sendmail** (the local MTA) or **SMTP** (an external mail server). Choosing SMTP enables the related Auth and SSL settings. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: Whether to set the email Return-Path header, and whether to use a specified address.
modal: Controls the Return-Path (bounce) address on outbound mail: **No**, **Yes** (use the sender address), or **Specified** (use the Return-Path Email below). Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The Return-Path (bounce) address used for outbound email.
modal: The address that receives bounce notifications for outbound mail. Applies only when **Set Return-Path** is set to Specified. Must be a valid email. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The authentication method used to connect to the SMTP server.
modal: The SMTP authentication method: **NONE**, **PLAIN**, or **LOGIN**. Applies only when Transport is set to SMTP. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The encryption used when connecting to the SMTP server.
modal: The connection security for SMTP: **None**, **SSL**, or **TLS**. Applies only when Transport is set to SMTP. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: Which store email identity sends Admin password forgot/reset emails.
modal: The sender identity for Admin 'forgot password' and reset emails — one of the **Store Email Addresses** identities (General Contact, Sales Representative, Customer Support, Custom 1/2).

comment: The Admin page shown first after a user signs in.
modal: The landing page displayed when an Admin user logs in, chosen from the available Admin menu destinations.

comment: Whether the Admin panel is served from a custom base URL.
modal: When **Yes**, the Admin uses a custom base URL instead of the default. Set the URL in the related field. Misconfiguration can lock you out of the Admin.

comment: Whether the Admin is reached at a custom path instead of the default.
modal: When **Yes**, the Admin is accessed under a custom path (e.g. `/myadmin`) rather than the default. Set the path in the related field. Misconfiguration can lock you out of the Admin.

comment: Adds a secret key to Admin URLs to protect against cross-site request forgery.
modal: When **Yes**, Admin URLs include a per-session secret key, a CSRF protection. Leave enabled unless a specific integration requires otherwise.

comment: Whether Admin usernames are matched case-sensitively at login.
modal: When **Yes**, Admin login treats the username as case-sensitive; when **No**, case is ignored.

comment: Whether charts are displayed on the Admin dashboard.
modal: When **Yes**, the Admin dashboard renders its sales/order charts. Disabling can reduce load on large stores where the chart queries are heavy.

comment: Removes index.php from storefront URLs using web server rewrites.
modal: When **Yes**, URLs are generated without `index.php`, relying on the web server's rewrite rules (e.g. Apache mod_rewrite or Nginx). Enable only when rewrites are configured on the server. Can differ per store view.

comment: The HTTP header used to detect that SSL is terminated by a load balancer or proxy.
modal: The request header (e.g. `X-Forwarded-Proto`) that the store reads to recognise HTTPS when SSL is offloaded to a proxy or load balancer rather than handled by the web server directly.

comment: The default storefront landing path used when no specific route is requested.
modal: The route the storefront falls back to for the home page when no path is given (typically `cms`). Can differ per website or store view.

comment: The path served when a requested URL matches no route (the 404 page).
modal: The internal path rendered when a URL cannot be matched to any route, i.e. the 'page not found' target. Can differ per website or store view.

comment: Validates that a session's client IP (REMOTE_ADDR) stays consistent, as anti-hijacking protection.
modal: When **Yes**, the session is bound to the client's REMOTE_ADDR and invalidated if it changes, guarding against session hijacking. May cause issues behind some proxies/NAT.

comment: Validates the HTTP_VIA header for the session, as anti-hijacking protection.
modal: When **Yes**, the session is tied to the request's HTTP_VIA header and invalidated if it changes. May cause issues behind some proxies.

comment: Validates the HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR header for the session, as anti-hijacking protection.
modal: When **Yes**, the session is tied to the request's HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR header and invalidated if it changes. May cause issues behind some proxies/load balancers.

comment: Validates the browser's HTTP_USER_AGENT for the session, as anti-hijacking protection.
modal: When **Yes**, the session is tied to the request's HTTP_USER_AGENT and invalidated if it changes, guarding against session hijacking.
